## Ledger Document

The common shape of a posted accounting document. It carries `docNo`, `date` (YYYY-MM-DD, the month it posts in), `memo`, `status` (`draft` until a subclass's `post` operation moves it to `posted`), `enteredBy` and `postedBy` (stamped by the realm). A subclass says what it posts by overriding `postings()`, which returns plain lines; `ledgerLines` is a computed `containsMany(PostingLine)` built from them with the document's `date` filled in, so every line it contributes to the general ledger is indexed and queryable. `totalMinor` is computed from `total()` (the sum of the debits by default) and `cardTitle` from `title()`.

Subclasses also override `facts()`, `state()` and `party()`; the isolated, embedded and fitted formats are rendered from these methods, so a new kind of document needs no templates of its own. The isolated view shows a "Posts to the ledger" section listing every line with its account code and its class, location, party and document tags.

```ts
import { LedgerDocument } from '@cardstack/catalog/cards/accounting/ledger-document';
```

```ts
class Refund extends LedgerDocument {
  postings() { return [/* debits and credits that balance */]; }
}
```

### Operations
The base type declares none. Each subclass declares its own `post`, which checks the document before it moves to `posted`.

### Non-goals
Does not enforce that debits equal credits itself; each subclass's `post` asserts what applies to it. Amounts are integer cents (`…Minor` fields) with no currency field; the ledger is single-currency. Accounts, parties and documents are referenced by text keys (an account code such as `1000`, a vendor or customer key, a document number), not by links.

### Example
No example ships: the base type has no instances of its own. See any subclass, such as Journal Entry or Ledger Invoice.
attributes.cardDescription: The base type for every posted accounting document: a dated, numbered record whose ledger lines are computed from its own posting rules.
